data.title: Hiring manager
data.content:
# Hiring manager

The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
data.summary: The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
controls: The requirements as written, and the ones only they know about
Who interviews and what they ask
The level a candidate is assessed at
Whether a split panel becomes a hire
blind_to: What the same candidate showed in rounds they did not attend
How the requirements read to someone outside the team
What the search is costing the people covering the gap
incentives: Avoid a bad hire, which is visible and attributed, more than a missed hire, which is neither
Fill the gap without the ramp-up cost of someone who needs teaching
Keep the team's own delivery on track while running the loop

specimens.label: The asymmetry that sets the bar

lines.text: A bad hire is visible for a year and attributed to the person who made it.
A missed hire is invisible and attributed to nobody.
Both are costly. Only one has a name on it.

specimens.reading: This is not a bias to be scolded out of anyone; it is an incentive with a shape. Several conservative-default mechanisms follow from it directly.
